review_method: Codex visual inspection performed again on all nine actual final 08485 stationary packaged-game screenshots; each image opened with view_image and exact identities cross-checked against the validated final 720p receipt. Previous 205bdd proof was not relabelled.
review_scope: All three world frame types in Apollo, SELENE and Mars at 1280x720. Nine images visually inspected; this does not visually certify all 120 staged images.

frames.name: world-rover-mounted
observations: The rover and forward terrain are visible; the previously observed Intrepid strut occlusion is absent in this final packaged stationary view.
Chassis, seat and wheels are visible; no player-mesh clipping is apparent in this frame.
Support card and radio overlay cover part of the lower vehicle; the deliberately hidden seated player leaves an empty-looking proxy seat.

frames.name: world-magnifier-cartridge
observations: The magnifier aperture is centred on the crosshair and the front TRAINING-01 label reads forwards.
The target remains visible; the support card overlays its lower face and handle.
The ring is visibly faceted and no hand grip is shown; this remains authored proxy presentation.

frames.name: world-sampler-package
observations: The front sampler/package body, cyan label panel and wheels are visible.
No severe terrain burial or player-model clipping is apparent in this reviewed still.
The robot and nearby rover remain simple box/cylinder authored proxies; the support card covers part of the lower sampler.

remaining_limits: Visuals remain authored training proxies, not replicas certified by NASA.
The magnifier has a faceted ring and no visible gripping hand in these frames.
World labels are small/dark in some SELENE/Mars views; the HUD card occludes lower equipment geometry.
The mounted player is intentionally hidden rather than represented by a seated animated driver.
Stationary screenshots do not demonstrate driving, camera transitions, wheel animation smoothness, safe exits or FPS. Functional and performance evidence is recorded separately.
